utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated. Mr. Thomas, looking at the witness's statement or testimony when he testified, I don't see his first name, could you make sure we get a first name, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I will do that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Colonel, could you begin, please, by giving us your full name?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: My full name is Eelco Christian Martin Jodocus Koster.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER

utterances.text: And what is your current rank?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER

utterances.text: Your Honours, could we please have 65 ter 09353 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Colonel, do you recognize this as a transcript of testimony that you gave in a Rule 61 hearing before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity yesterday to review that transcript?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I had that opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Are you able to confirm for Their Honours that what is contained in the transcript is true and correct to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And if I were to ask you the same questions again, would your answers be the same?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if that could please be admitted as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Transcript is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P383.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If we could please have 65 ter 9354 on the screen. And perhaps, Your Honours, if we could have page 2, which might be of more assistance than page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Colonel, do you recognise what you see on the screen now as the transcript of your testimony in the Popovic case before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS

utterances.text: That's admitted as a Prosecution exhibit. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P384.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I now have a summary prepared of the testimony that is comprised within those two transcripts. If I could be permitted to read that into the record at this point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Lieutenant Koster arrived at the Dutch Battalion, DutchBat base in Potocari in January 1995 as a first lieutenant assigned as the battalion's logistics officer. On 11 July 1995 Lieutenant Koster was in command of approximately 30 DutchBat soldiers who were posted outside the UN compound in Potocari to receive an expected arrival of refugees from Srebrenica. The refugees arrived from around 1500 hours onward on foot, in UN trucks and armoured personnel carriers. The refugees were terrified, afraid and looking for help. Lieutenant Koster and his unit directed the refugees initially to take shelter inside a disused bus station near the UN compound. Some refugees were also let into the UN compound itself. Lieutenant Koster estimated that by the end of the day there were approximately 15.000 civilians who arrived and were gathered outside the UN compound, and a further 4 to 5.000 people who were placed inside the compound. On 12 July 1995, at around 1300 hours, Bosnian Serb soldiers arrived at lieutenant Koster's position, remaining behind a red and white tape that the DutchBat soldiers had placed as a demarcation line. At around 1600 hours, more VRS troops arrived. Then, General Mladic arrived at Lieutenant Koster's position. General Mladic refused to say what his intentions were and refused to report to the DutchBat commander at the compound. General Mladic stated that he was in charge there, he would do as he pleased, that Lieutenant Koster would see what was going to happen and that it would be best for the DutchBat soldiers to cooperate. The DutchBat soldiers were severely outnumbered. General Mladic addressed the refugees accompanied by a camera team. At this time Lieutenant Koster saw that buses had arrived. He asked General Mladic again what he was going to do with the refugees, to which General Mladic replied that he would evacuate them to another location. Bosnian Serb soldiers then told the refugees to board the buses. The Bosnian Serb soldiers pushed the refugees to go to the buses and get inside them, overfilling the buses with them. Before the buses were loaded men of fighting age were separated and placed inside a nearby house, after their belongings had been removed from them. Lieutenant Koster and his men stayed with the remaining refugees on the evening of 12 July. During the night groups of Bosnian Serb soldiers returned and at gunpoint forced the majority of Lieutenant Koster's unit to surrender their weapon, bulletproof vests and helmets. During the night the DutchBat soldiers continued to help those sick and wounded who needed medical help. On the morning of 13 July 1995, buses arrived at around 0700 hours and the removal of refugees by the Bosnian Serb soldiers resumed, lasting until approximately 1800 hours. By that time all the refugees exempt for some wounded, had been removed. The men who had earlier been separated and placed in the nearby house had also gone. And that concludes the summary, Your Honours. Your Honours, there are some matters of clarification and amplification from Colonel Koster's testimony to which I would like to refer him. They involve playing clips, video clips taken from 65 ter Exhibit 4 -- sorry 04559. There are six such clips, Your Honours, of varying duration.

utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.text: The only problem, Mr. Thomas, is that if Lieutenant Koster did not mention that in his previous testimony, why do you want to introduce that testimony now? utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And if you are saying the picture here tends to contradict what he said and he was not asked to clarify that previously, why do you want to clarify it today?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If Your Honours could give me a moment, I'll search for the appropriate passage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please do. That was actually the objection, or the request from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS

utterances.text: We have seen that on the clip. We have seen him saying to the UN people, I don't care less what you think, I'm in control here. And then we see him being kind to the civilians.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Well, I can't describe each and every one of the objects, but I assume that they were the belongings of the male refugees. I saw them being brought there, and the men were ordered to leave the things that they had with them over there. In any case, those things were taken away from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Colonel, can you tell us who the men are in general terms who we see sitting on the balcony of the white house?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise them as the male refugees who were separated by the Bosnian Serb soldiers from the rest of the refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If we could tender that clip as an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P390.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Finally, could I have Exhibit 65 ter 07393 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Colonel, do you recognise that as an aerial photograph of Potocari?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do you see the UN compound? Is that represented anywhere in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. The UN compound appears in the middle and near the bottom of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: What I'd like you to do, Colonel, is I'll ask for you to be provided with an electronic pen, please, and could you draw a circle around the buildings that constitute, or the area that constitutes the UN compound, please.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. And within that circle, could you please write the letters "UNC"?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You described in your testimony or referred in your testimony to a bus shelter or a bus station, I'm sorry, where the civilians took shelter for some time. Is that depicted anywhere on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Absolutely. It's located near the top of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could you circle that, please, for us.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And please just write the "BS" in there.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And you have spoken just now of the white house, is that depicted anywhere in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could you circle that for us, please, and mark "WH."

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: How far would the white house be from the bus shelter, from the bus station?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: At most, a few hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel. Your Honours, could this also be tendered as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 65 ter 07393 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the marked photograph will be Exhibit P391.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And thank you, Your Honours, that concludes my evidence in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Koster, good afternoon or good evening. My name is Novak Lukic and I'm the counsel who will be asking you some questions on behalf of the Defence team of Mr. Perisic. In relation to the events in Srebrenica, you testified on two previous occasions in the Popovic case in the year 2006, and you also testified in the Krstic case, or rather, when the indictment against Mr. Mladic and Mr. Karadzic was being confirmed in 1996 you also testified. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before your testimony, you made a solemn declaration and promised to tell the truth, and you also made several written statements and gave interviews with various -- to various officials of the OTP of The Hague and other institutions where you also describe the events that took place in Srebrenica in 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And although you did not have to make a solemn declaration when making written statements as you did before the Court, you always put forward events that were correct and true to the best of your knowledge and recollection; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I described the events as I remembered them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You arrived on the territory of the Potocari enclave sometime in January 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would I be right in concluding that from January until the fall of the enclave, you had relatively frequent contacts with members of the Muslim military forces?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: No, I hardly had any contact at all with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you did describe some of these contacts in your testimony. May I ask you whether you remember how many contacts you had with members of the Muslim military forces in total?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: At the end of my period, I did have contact with the Muslim forces and I'd have to take a guess. I estimate there were about five such times.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will define these men as Muslim fighters. You saw that they wore different sort of clothing. Some were in civilian clothes, some had parts of uniforms, others had entire uniforms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As for the weapons they carried, you saw them carrying Kalashnikov automatic rifles, mortars and you also saw that they had Motorolas and other radio equipment?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: If that's a question, the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Muslim fighters banned the members of your unit to enter one part of the enclave and patrol there, you were prohibited from going there by the Muslim forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That did hold true for a very brief period.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That was in January 1995?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In January 1995 were the members of your unit prohibited from patrolling a part of the enclave by the members of the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I hesitate to interrupt my learned friend, but this obviously isn't a matter that arises from evidence in chief, nor is it a matter which appears to go to the credibility of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Complying with your guidelines, Your Honours, I wish to put certain questions which are of a general relevance to the Defence in order to show that the enclave which was designated a protected area by the United Nations was not actually such before the fall of the enclave. These questions are relevant to the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which part of the guideline are you complying with, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm referring to the scope of cross-examination referred to in the guidelines, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. Just a moment. Paragraph 8: [In English] "... when the witness is able to give evidence related to the case for the cross-examinating party." [Interpretation] That's Rule 90(h)(i).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. The objection is overruled.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question was, do you remember that already in January 1995, the members of your unit were prohibited from patrolling all parts of the enclave, you were banned from entering certain parts of the enclave by the members of the Muslim military forces?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I remember that at the start of my deployment, a certain area -- that the Muslim side tried to screen off a certain area and told us that we weren't allowed to enter that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the reason for this an incident in which Major Franken and 8 soldiers from your battalion were held hostage, or rather, were they held hostage because they refused to obey that decision by the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I know that armed forces from our side were held hostage temporarily. That's the only thing I can remember. I don't remember the names or the number of UN soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But do you remember the incident that caused them to be held hostage, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I remember the incident. We resisted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You resisted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was the incident as described previously. I believe that was the Bandera triangle, it concerned the Bandera triangle, which was in our enclave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you say the incident that was described previously, described by who, when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise, I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said at page 70 line 12: "It was the incident as described previously." I'm trying to find -- and then you say: "I believe that was the Bandera triangle." I'm asking, incident described previously by whom and when? Are you talking about the description by this lawyer or are you talking about some other description?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about the description as Mr. Lukic just presented to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have in e-court document 1D00-2700. That is Mr. Koster's statement which he made to the investigators of the OTP of The Hague on the 25th and 26th of September 1995. It's page 2 in the B/C/S version and also page 2 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And let me read the paragraph so that, Mr. Koster, I can jog your memory. I'll read it in English. Yes, thank you. I'm reading the last paragraph. And I will read in the Serbian language. "At the end of January 1995, the Muslim fighters wanted us to --" could we scroll down, please. "To keep out of a certain part of the enclave. Major Franken and 8 soldiers out of the reconnaissance platoon endeavoured to enter this area in order to enforce the condition of freedom of movement. When they did so, they were taken hostage." Would you scroll down a little more, please. "I believe that Zulfo, a subordinate commander in the Muslim forces, was responsible for this hostage taking. I never saw this Zulfo. He was one of Naser Oric's commanders. I later heard that there was a power struggle going on between these two men." This statement, Mr. Koster, was taken from you in 1995, and I assume that your memory then was better and fresher. Does this jog your memory and is what it says here correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you answer that question, do you recognise that as your statement, sir? Do you recognise that statement at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I recognise this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then you may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise for not verifying this first.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Koster, do you remember now the reason why this group of men was detained by the Muslim fighters, and do you remember this event taking place in the way you describe it here?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, I do remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now move on to the events of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you do so, what do you want to do with the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't wish to tender it into evidence, Your Honour. I only wanted to quote part of it to the witness and that's sufficient for my purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the 10th of July 1995, when you were setting out to direct the refugees you expected to be coming from Srebrenica, you saw some Muslim fighters in a house where they had set up a subcommand. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also heard that there was fighting between the Muslim fighters and the Serbian fighters on the 12th and on the 13th of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: In that period I did indeed hear an exchange of fire from the surrounding hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that from the middle of June in the village of Potocari, there were many armed Muslims, and they could no longer be kept under control, you could no longer tell them to lay down their weapons because more and more of these armed men were gathering in the village itself?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I'd like to know, are you talking about Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, we did indeed see increasing numbers of armed men walking around. And in the end there were so many of them that we could no longer take their weapons away from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you are referring to Muslim fighters now; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I'm referring to the male Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, very well. Your battalion numbered about 200 members at that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, it must have been about approximately 200 members.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also heard that there was shelling in the night between the 11th and 12th of July, but no shells landed in those areas where the refugees had already arrived?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, if you are referring to where the refugees were gathered, the shells fell in between the houses. I couldn't tell whether or not there were any refugees there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But in the area where the refugees were gathered together, no shells landed; is that correct? Where the first wave of refugees gathered, none of them were hit by a shell; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: From what I could see, the refugees that were near me were not hit by the shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember having heard on the following day that any civilians had been killed or wounded by that shelling?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: No, I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You did not expect such large numbers of refugees to arrive in Potocari on the 11th and the 12th of July, did you? You were surprised by the situation and the number of refugees who arrived?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that point in time, you didn't know that some sort of evacuation would be organised, did you? When those people arrived, you did not know they would be evacuated, did you?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Evacuated by whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I was getting at. When those civilians arrived from Srebrenica to Potocari, was there any talk of any kind of evacuation of those people at the time when they arrived?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Thank you. No, and first all we spoke about was accommodating the refugees and we would see about evacuation later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We saw that you met General Mladic and you testified about that meeting. He informed you personally that he wished to evacuate those refugees?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You did not want those refugees to be taken away to be evacuated until he told you exactly where they would be evacuated to and that they would be safe?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You had no reason to doubt what he told you, that they would be taken somewhere and that they would be safe?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I was not certain of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the course of your meeting with him, did you have any reason to suspect he would not be taking those refugees to a safe territory?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: We were there to protect the Muslim population against the Bosnian Serb soldiers, and that was cause for me to doubt the certainty that he would indeed relocate them in a proper manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When he informed you that he would carry out the evacuation of those civilians to a safe area and that nothing would happen to them, did you inform your superiors of what he had told you?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I reported that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you inform them of your doubts as to what he said, that is that he would safely take them to Kladanj?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: At that point, I didn't know that he would take them to Kladanj. I merely reported that the refugees were going to be evacuated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But did you report your doubts and your suspicions that he would not do this in a safe and proper way?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: All I remember is that I expressed concern about this evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who did you inform of this?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I informed the operations room.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any instructions from the operations room as to how you should proceed, what course you should follow next?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what were you told to do?

utterances.speaker: EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
utterances.text: I was instructed to indicate to General Mladic that he should contact Karremans, my commander, and that until that time I should not cooperate with the evacuation of the refugees until there was more certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we break off now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed we can. It's about time. Sir, we are not finished with your testimony. Can you please come back tomorrow at quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon, and let me just say to you that now that you are in the witness box, I'm sure you know this, you are not supposed to discuss the case with anybody until you have finished testifying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry. My learned friend and I were proceeding on the basis that we would be able to conclude Colonel Koster's evidence today. There is a difficulty with Dutch interpretation being available tomorrow. It is available on Thursday but I've also spoken to Colonel Koster. He would be prepared to -- he has a pretty good command of English and he would be prepared to continue in English but I just simply flag that if any problems arise in that respect tomorrow, Your Honour, that we don't have Dutch interpretation available, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, but if he prefers to testify in Dutch, then he must testify in Dutch.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: That would be my preference certainly and his, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In that case, then are you suggesting we postpone to Thursday?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then we'll adjourn to Thursday. Is it possible to sit in the morning rather than in the afternoon. Judge David would be available on that day, Lukic and Lukic is not sitting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we sit on Thursday morning? Is it possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: It's certainly causes the Prosecution no difficulties, sir, but it's not something I've specifically asked Colonel Koster.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And the other people, the interpreters and everybody and the Defence. How does it suit you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no problem with that. I just wanted to inform Your Honours that I will take half an hour or 40 minutes at the most for my -- for the continuation of my cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Would it be convenient for you to come in the morning on Thursday, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll be here Thursday morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess also for our interpreters at the back. Thank you very much. I see smiles, which I interpret to mean yes. Thanks. Okay, we will then stand adjourned to Thursday morning at 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm told we'll have to go to Courtroom I. I'm sure someone will show you where Courtroom I is. It's at 9.00 in the morning on Thursday. Thank you so much. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: be reconvened on Thursday, the 4th day of December, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 24

procedural_notes.text: WITNESS:  EELCO CHRISTIAN MARTIN JODOCUS KOSTER
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.04 p.m. to
